title: The New Zealand Artist Will Burton
titleZh: 新西兰艺术家威尔·伯顿

parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Part four. You will hear part of a lecture about the contemporary New Zealand artist, Will Burton. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome back to this series of lectures on contemporary New Zealand artists. Today, Will Burton.

Will Burton stands out from the other artists we've considered in these lectures because of his choice of materials. From a young age, Burton has enjoyed making art from rubbish and waste. Now, today, this might not be thought particularly unusual. Today, lots of artists are doing this sort of thing. But at the time when Burton started using this approach, the nineteen fifties, the art world in this country was traditional, to put it politely, and his ideas were highly original. It's for this reason that I want to focus today's lecture on Will Burton's early years when he formed his pioneering approach to art. Burton grew up in the Wellington seaside suburb of Moa Point in the years after the Second World War, and both the place and the time were important influences. He initially spent a lot of time painting, but eventually gave this up because it placed too many limits on his imagination. It was then that he started to explore new materials, and in particular, the idea of using rubbish for creative purposes. Some of his first pieces were made from waste he found in the domestic environment. So, for example, he did a series of sculptures using glass bottles, but he was also attracted to anything made from plastic, which was then relatively new and exotic. Another feature of Moa Point was the beach, and this became an important influence on his work. Here he found examples of what he considered to be natural waste, things which nature had discarded, if you like, things like shells, for example, which he often used in his art. Of course, those of you who are familiar with Moa Point will know that the suburb has one other prominent feature, the large rubbish dump, and it was here, perhaps more than anywhere else, that Burton liked to hunt for materials to use in his art. He collected all sorts of things from the dump, as you might imagine, but in particular, he was inspired by any sort of electrical equipment, which in the nineteen fifties was just beginning to be introduced to many homes. Now, it's perhaps not surprising that most of the artwork he produced during this period has not survived, but the Wellington Museum has managed to hold on to a number of pieces.

One of the things he often found at the dump were old light bulbs, and on display in the museum today is a wonderful series of photographs Burton took of these bulbs.

When he left his parents' home, Will Burton studied at the Canterbury School of Fine Arts. Here he developed those more formal skills normally associated with students of fine art. For example, the ability to draw in pencil, and in fact, produced many wonderful portraits of his friends, often on a very large scale. But of course, he also pursued his own ideas. In particular, we can see in his student years the beginnings of Burton's interest in movement and motion. Indeed, I believe that had he wanted to, Burton might easily have found success creating movies, such is his skill in working with movement.

Another of his great interests in life also began when Burton was at art school. Like many students in those days, he spent the summer holidays going around the country and then ventured further afield to Australia and Southeast Asia, and this passion for travel has stayed with him throughout his life.

Returning to his art, what other themes are of importance? So much of Burton's output explores the way in which ordinary objects can seem to change. One thing in particular that drives his work is the way appearances change depending on how much light is available. Another point is that throughout his career, Burton has been an astute observer of modern society and often a highly critical one. And there is often a wonderfully light and playful character to Burton's work. For example, he often uses sections of text in his photographs or sculptures to express his sense of humor. However, this alone would not be enough to secure his importance among our contemporary artists. Ultimately, what gives his work its depth is the way the artist so often expresses his sense of loss for those people and places which he will not see again. Well now, if there are any questions, please don't hesitate...

That is the end of part four. You now have one minute to check your answers to part four.

analyses.content: 录音中提到他起初花了很多时间在绘画（painting）上，但因为限制了想象力而最终放弃了。
注意听到“initially”对应题干的“started with”，“gave this up”对应题干的转折，不要因为没听到完全一样的词就错失答案。
He initially spent a lot of time painting, but eventually gave this up because it placed too many limits on his imagination.
录音里举例说明他用家里的废弃物做雕塑，先提到了玻璃瓶（glass bottles），接着用“but also”引出了另一种并列材料塑料（plastic）。
你可能会听到“bottles”就想写下来，但题干已经给出了“glass”，你需要填并列的另一种材质“plastic”。

Some of his first pieces were made from waste he found in the domestic environment. So, for example, he did a series of sculptures using glass bottles, but he was also attracted to anything made from plastic, which was then relatively new and exotic.
录音提到他发现了自然废弃物（natural waste），并紧接着用“like... for example”举例说是贝壳（shells）。
你可能会因为录音里插入了“things which nature had discarded, if you like”这句较长的补充说明而走神，一定要耐心听到后面的举例词“shells”。
Here he found examples of what he considered to be natural waste, things which nature had discarded, if you like, things like shells, for example, which he often used in his art.
录音中说到他从垃圾场收集各种东西，特别提到（in particular）他受到各种电子的（electrical）设备启发。
录音里的“in particular”完美对应题干的“especially”，听到这个信号词就要准备抓取后面的核心修饰词“electrical”，别错填成名词“equipment”，因为题干后面已经有“items”了。

Of course, those of you who are familiar with Moa Point will know that the suburb has one other prominent feature, the large rubbish dump, and it was here, perhaps more than anywhere else, that Burton liked to hunt for materials to use in his art. He collected all sorts of things from the dump, as you might imagine, but in particular, he was inspired by any sort of electrical equipment, which in the nineteen fifties was just beginning to be introduced to many homes.
录音提到博物馆今天展出了一系列他拍摄这些旧灯泡的照片（photographs）。
这里的语序出现了倒装和替换，录音先说了博物馆展出照片，再说是拍灯泡的，你要根据题干的结构“... of old light bulbs”迅速锁定核心名词“photographs”。

Now, it's perhaps not surprising that most of the artwork he produced during this period has not survived, but the Wellington Museum has managed to hold on to a number of pieces. One of the things he often found at the dump were old light bulbs, and on display in the museum today is a wonderful series of photographs Burton took of these bulbs.
录音先说了他发展了更为正式的技能（formal skills），随后举例（For example）提到了用铅笔（pencil）画画的能力。
这里的干扰信息不多，主要考察你对“For example”引导的具体技能的抓取，听到“draw in”后面就是答案，不要忽略细节错填成后面的“portraits”。

Here he developed those more formal skills normally associated with students of fine art. For example, the ability to draw in pencil, and in fact, produced many wonderful portraits of his friends, often on a very large scale.
录音中提到如果他愿意的话，他本可以轻易在制作电影（movies）方面获得成功，这对应了题干的“备选职业（alternative career）”。
题干的“alternative career”在录音中被替换成了“might easily have found success creating...（本可以轻易在……获得成功）”，你要能识别出这种整句语义上的同义替换，并抓取核心名词。

In particular, we can see in his student years the beginnings of Burton's interest in movement and motion. Indeed, I believe that had he wanted to, Burton might easily have found success creating movies, such is his skill in working with movement.
录音在描述完他四处游历的经历后，总结说这种对旅行（travel）的热爱伴随了他一生。
录音前面的“going around the country”和“ventured further afield”都是在描述游历的具体过程，直到最后才用“passion for travel”总结，你要耐心听到最后对应“lifelong interest”的总结句。

Another of his great interests in life also began when Burton was at art school. Like many students in those days, he spent the summer holidays going around the country and then ventured further afield to Australia and Southeast Asia, and this passion for travel has stayed with him throughout his life.
录音里明确说到他经常在作品中使用文字（sections of text）来表达他的幽默感（humor）。
题干的“written words”被替换成了“sections of text”，听到这里就要警觉，紧跟其后的“express his sense of”直接引出了正确答案。
And there is often a wonderfully light and playful character to Burton's work. For example, he often uses sections of text in his photographs or sculptures to express his sense of humor.
录音最后总结说，赋予他作品深度（depth）的是他经常表达出的对不再见到的人和地的失落感（loss）。
这道题的结构非常直接，“gives his work its depth”和“expresses his sense of”几乎原词重现，只要跟上进度就不会漏掉，唯独需要注意拼写不要出错。

However, this alone would not be enough to secure his importance among our contemporary artists. Ultimately, what gives his work its depth is the way the artist so often expresses his sense of loss for those people and places which he will not see again.
